parsed.explanation: Combined regime: federal entry, passport, facilities and custody exposures remain operative and severe if triggered, while the division provides documented, strong local protections for public accommodation, identity documents, hate-crime reporting and shielded care, including for minors. No local bathroom ban, youth-care ban, or documented local police targeting is in the dossier. The unenforced same-sex provisions are a dead-letter secondary factor since 1974 and do not drive the rating. Federal uncertainty and document-discrepancy screening keep the case well below the strongest-protection tier but above a generic national average.

entry_documents.exposure: Federal binary sex definition; X-marker passports not newly processed, only M/F; 2025 cable instructs refusal where document discrepancy casts reasonable doubt and consideration of permanent fraud ineligibility if wilful misrepresentation is suspected.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X passports remain valid until expiration; division issues local X licences/ID and self-declared birth-certificate amendments without surgery.
entry_documents.interaction: State document and accommodation law does not cancel federal entry screening; a federal discrepancy encounter can precede admission to the protective division.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Federal immigration custody reports of forced labour, beatings, solitary confinement and severe sexual abuse of trans men; federal prison policies from 2026 cut hair, remove hormones and substitute psychiatric treatment, with reporting stopped.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: No division custody abuse documented; federal rescue and refusal remedies exist through litigation and consular processes, but status of challenges is unresolved.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: If federal detention follows entry refusal or investigation, birth-sex, care-denial and abuse exposures follow the traveller despite state protections.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Federal order bars government-funded single-sex facilities congruent with gender identity; 21 state/provinces have mapped bans, and 4 make some use criminal in specified circumstances, illustrated by a 2025 trespass arrest elsewhere.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Division public-accommodation protection since 2016, retained by 67.8% referendum in 2018, covers hotels, restaurants, shops and transport; no division facility ban documented.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Division law protects state/private facilities but, absent documented pre-emption, does not cancel federal facility rules in federal buildings or funded facilities.

care_services.exposure: Federal orders describe minors' affirming care as mutilation, freeze funding, propose barring public insurance under 18, and DOJ subpoenaed hospital records for patients under 19; several orders are blocked or enjoined.
care_services.protection: Division shield law since 2022 protects patients and providers from civil/criminal liability for care lawful here but banned at home; 2022 law codifies affirming-care protections.
care_services.interaction: Shield mitigates home-state and division liability, not documented federal funding, insurance or investigative exposure; operative federal status is partly uncertain.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Federal counterterrorism strategy prioritises groups described as radically pro-transgender; DOJ memo uses radical gender ideology in extremism context; school inquiry/prosecution direction covers pronoun use for minors.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Memo never uses the phrase as reward criterion and strategy says disagreement alone is not targeted; division hate-crime law includes gender identity since 2012 with public reporting and a task force.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Federal framing raises discovery and investigation risk at national interfaces, while division law supplies local recourse for bias crimes and discrimination.

minors_guardians.exposure: Parent/guardian may face federal school investigation, teacher-prosecution and youth-care funding/insurance restrictions concerning a travelling minor; proposed rules remain unresolved and some orders are enjoined.
minors_guardians.protection: No division youth-care ban documented; shield and codified-care laws, conversion-therapy ban for minors since 2019, and anti-bullying procedures protect care and schooling locally.
minors_guardians.interaction: A family seeking lawful local care is shielded at state level, but federal records, funding or school inquiries can still interact with the journey.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Not documented. No division-specific pattern of trans street violence, police harassment or extortion is provided; national advisories and hostile federal rhetoric are contextual, not local incident rates.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Division anti-discrimination law in employment, housing, credit and public accommodation, plus gender-identity hate-crime coverage and reporting machinery, are documented operative protections.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Local recourse is stronger than a thin-data silence, but absence of local incident data is not treated as proof of zero street risk.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Passport suit remains challenged after November 2025 Supreme Court allowed restrictions to take effect; several federal orders are blocked or enjoined and their current operative scope is uncertain.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Division protections have electoral durability and documented legislative votes; national hate-crime statute covers gender identity, and civil-liberties litigation is active.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: State remedies do not resolve federal entry, passport or custody questions; traveller exposure depends on which federal measures are in force when travelling.

anchor_checks.comparison: Far higher than 0.25: no local raids, extortion, routine custody or short imprisonment for presentation is documented here, while division protections and a functioning hate-crime/reporting system operate. Federal custody abuse is serious but is not shown as routine local enforcement.

Higher than 0.55 because the division adds explicit public-accommodation, document, hate-crime and shield-care protections, unlike a system relying mainly on slow discretionary appeals. The shared feature is federal secondary screening and possible refused admission for document discrepancy.

Similar-to-higher: like 0.65, care or document friction can be remedied and imprisonment for identity is not the documented local outcome. Stronger local statute, referendum durability and shield law push above 0.65, but federal custody and facility exposures prevent the 0.85 tier.

Lower than 0.85: 0.85 has no credible imprisonment pathway and only occasional friction, whereas here federal binary-passport rules, discrepancy-based refusal with lifetime-ineligibility consideration, federal facilities restrictions and documented federal custody abuse remain operative or uncertain.

parsed.synthesis: The traveller encounters two interacting systems. Federal screening can out and refuse a traveller whose documents mismatch presentation, with possible investigation and severe federal custody if detained; federal facilities and minor-care measures add further exposure. Once in the division, however, public-accommodation law retained by referendum, self-declared local documents, hate-crime reporting, and a care shield create real local protection, including for families. That protective operating regime materially raises safety above the national context, but it does not pre-empt federal entry, facilities or custody. Hence a reduced-risk, not low-risk, rating.
